name: Canvas multi-frame animation workflow creates bouncing ball with onion skinning and custom frame holds
description: Verify drawing a multi-frame animation sequence from scratch in the Studio: drawing a solid colored ball at apex on Frame 1, adding Frame 2 with onion skinning, drawing squashed contact on Frame 3, configuring frame hold durations, setting loop mode to BOUNCE, and playing.

planSteps.description: Select the Ellipse tool (press O), ensure shape mode is 'Shape: Filled Solid', and draw a solid circular ball near the top of the canvas on Frame 1
Select Flood Fill (press G), select a bright red color, and fill the ball solidly
Verify the high resting ball is visible on Frame 1
Click the 'Onion Skin' button in the bottom timeline bar to enable ghost previews
Click the 'Frame' button in the timeline to create Frame 2
Verify the Frame 1 ball appears as a translucent onion skin ghost
On Frame 2, select Ellipse, draw an elongated falling ball in the middle canvas, and fill with the same red color
Click the 'Frame' button in the timeline to create Frame 3
On Frame 3, draw a wide, flattened ball squashed against the bottom floor line and fill with red
Change the active frame duration input on Frame 3 from 100ms to 250ms (for ground impact hold)
Verify the Frame #3 thumbnail pill reflects the 250ms duration
Click the Loop Mode button in the bottom timeline until it switches to 'BOUNCE' (ping-pong playback)
Click the 'PLAY' button in the timeline
Verify the timeline actively plays and bounces forward (1 -> 2 -> 3) and backward (3 -> 2 -> 1) without tearing or dropping frames
